posts.title: Plain Language Handwashing Guides for Employees With Dyslexia
posts.summary: Using plain language and readable guides makes handwashing and glove use accessible for employees with dyslexia, improving compliance and safety.

posts.title: Pictorial Checklists Aid Employees With Mental Health Conditions In Cleaning Protocols
posts.summary: Visual checklists and color coding make cleaning and sanitizing tasks more accessible for employees with mental health conditions while improving overall kitchen safety.

posts.title: Tactile Thermometer Guides for Blind Employees
posts.summary: I argue that breaking temperature checks into tactile steps enables blind employees to perform food safety tasks reliably.

posts.title: Color Coded Cleaning Guides for Employees With Mobility Disabilities
posts.summary: Using color coded visual guides makes cleaning and sanitizing tasks accessible and reliable for employees with mobility disabilities.

posts.title: Visual Checklists Support Deaf Employees in Personal Hygiene
posts.summary: Using clear visual checklists helps Deaf employees follow personal hygiene protocols and report illness reliably.

posts.title: Captioned Video Modules for Allergen Safety Training
posts.summary: Captioned video instruction can make allergen safety training accessible to Deaf and hard of hearing foodservice employees.

posts.title: Helping Employees with Intellectual Disabilities Speak Up About Food Safety
posts.summary: I argue that teaching employees with intellectual disabilities how and when to report a food safety problem is as important as teaching the task itself.

posts.title: Manager Confidence Shapes Inclusive Food Safety Training
posts.summary: I argue that inclusive food safety training depends heavily on whether managers feel prepared to train employees with disabilities.

posts.title: Teaching Temperature Checks to Employees with Learning Disabilities
posts.summary: I argue that temperature checks can be taught to employees with learning disabilities by replacing number heavy rules with color, matching, and practice.

posts.title: Skill Based Credentials Can Open Food Safety Certification to Workers with Disabilities
posts.summary: I argue that short credentials earned by demonstrating one food safety skill at a time can give workers with disabilities a fair way to show what they know.

posts.title: Neurodiversity and Food Safety Training
posts.summary: Food safety training works better for neurodivergent employees when it offers clear structure, flexible delivery, and a predictable environment.

posts.title: Supported Employment Partnerships Can Strengthen Kitchen Staffing
posts.summary: I argue that partnerships with supported employment programs give kitchens a dependable source of workers with disabilities who arrive with training support already in place.

posts.title: Tactile and Audible Food Safety Cues for Blind Staff
posts.summary: I argue that tactile and audible signals can make food safety standards usable for blind and low vision kitchen workers.

posts.title: Preparing Hospitality Students to Train Employees with Disabilities
posts.summary: I argue that hospitality programs should teach future managers how to deliver food safety training to employees with disabilities, not only how to pass a food safety exam.

posts.title: Using Familiar Foods to Teach Food Safety to Employees with Intellectual Disabilities
posts.summary: I argue that food safety lessons built around foods and routines employees already know are easier for employees with intellectual disabilities to learn and remember.

posts.title: Clear Food Safety Guidance for Busy Kitchens
posts.summary: I argue that simplifying food safety instructions makes compliance more realistic for frontline staff.

posts.title: Training That Leaves No One Behind
posts.summary: Why food safety training has to be designed for every worker on the line, not just the average one.
